blockMcqs.question: What two parts must every recursive function have?
options: A loop and a counter
A base case and a recursive case
A stack and a queue
A prune step and an undo step
blockMcqs.explanation: Without a base case the descent never stops; the recursive case must shrink the input.

blockMcqs.question: What most commonly causes infinite recursion?
options: Too many parameters per call
A missing or unreachable base case
Returning before the recursive call
Using a global variable
blockMcqs.explanation: If nothing stops the descent, frames pile up until the stack overflows.

blockMcqs.question: Why is naive recursive Fibonacci exponential?
options: Each call allocates a new array
The base case runs too often
It recomputes the same subproblems repeatedly
Stack frames are never freed
blockMcqs.explanation: Overlapping subproblems like fib(2) are solved many times; caching them makes it linear.

blockMcqs.question: What are the three core steps of the backtracking template?
options: Sort, search, return
Choose, explore, un-choose
Push, pop, peek
Split, solve, merge
blockMcqs.explanation: The undo step lets a single shared state be reused across branches without copying.

blockMcqs.question: How do combinations avoid duplicate sets like {1,2} and {2,1}?
options: By sorting each set before recording
By tracking a used-set of elements
By only picking indices after the current one
By pruning sets larger than k
blockMcqs.explanation: Restricting to later indices means a reordering can never be generated twice.

blockMcqs.question: When should you prefer iteration over recursion?
options: For shallow tree traversals
For deep, essentially linear work
Whenever a base case exists
For divide-and-conquer problems
blockMcqs.explanation: Deep linear recursion can exhaust the finite call stack and crash.

blockMcqs.question: Does pruning improve the worst-case big-O of a backtracking search?
options: Yes, it makes it polynomial
Usually no, but it cuts real runtime a lot
Only when the input is sorted
Yes, it removes the recursion entirely
blockMcqs.explanation: An adversarial input may prune nothing, so the exponential worst case stands.

blockMcqs.question: What is catastrophic backtracking?
options: A recursion with no base case
Exponential-time regex matching on hostile input
Losing the shared state after undo
A stack overflow during parsing
blockMcqs.explanation: A bad pattern explores too many paths, the root cause of ReDoS outages.

blockMcqs.question: Why must you record a copy of the shared candidate, not a reference?
options: Copying is faster than referencing
References cannot be stored in a list
All entries would point to the same mutated list
It avoids triggering the base case
blockMcqs.explanation: The shared list keeps changing, so every stored reference ends up identical and empty.
